newsitem.title: UK: HSBC MADE NO SPECULATION IN ASIAN FX.
newsitem.headline: HSBC MADE NO SPECULATION IN ASIAN FX.

text.p: HSBC Holdings, Asia's biggest bank, took no speculative positions in the recent currency turmoil which affected Thailand, Indonesia and the Philippines, its Chief Executive John Bond said on Wednesday.
"We took no proprietary speculative positions against any of the currencies involved," Bond said in an interview. "We try to make our money in the old fashioned way -- we earn it."
Bond said HSBC continued to make markets in a very volatile price environment and with higher volumes.
"Our results for the past three months in that part of the world have been within the normal range for our business," Bond added.
Earlier, Standard Chartered Plc said it had made substantial higher profits in the first half from foreign exchange dealing.

Income from foreign exchange rose 108 million stg in the first half from 80 million in the same period last year, helping raise the bank's Treasury profits to 103 million stg from 76 million stg last time.

"We've had a very good record on this in the last few months," StanChart chief executive Malcolm Williamson told Reuters. "You get daily ups and downs, but we've managed our book tightly and well and its continued through July."
A spokesman for Standard Chartered confirmed that the bank trades to protect its own positions but has at no time speculated against Asian currencies.
